title: PAT: Geometry-Aware Hard-Label Black-Box Adversarial Attacks on Text

problem.claim: Text adversarial attacks must operate when the victim model is black-box, only hard top-1 labels are available, and perturbations must preserve original semantics.

gap.claim: Text adversarial attacks remain challenging under the combined constraints of black-box access, hard labels, and semantic preservation.

contributions.claim: PAT is an adversarial attack method designed for the black-box, hard-label, semantic-preservation setting.
PAT models adversarial and non-adversarial prototypes to estimate semantic changes for replacement selection and generates high-quality adversarial samples.
PAT uses a geometry-aware iterative procedure to select replacement candidates that improve perturbation construction while minimally affecting original semantics.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe PAT as a novel adversarial attack method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On benchmark datasets and state-of-the-art models, the authors report that PAT outperforms existing text adversarial attacks in attack effectiveness and semantic preservation.
The authors report validating PAT against industry-leading natural language processing platforms in real-world settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Practical text adversarial attacks face black-box access, hard-label feedback, and semantic-preservation constraints.
The paper introduces PAT for attacking under all three constraints.
PAT uses adversarial and non-adversarial prototypes to estimate semantic changes and guide replacement selection.
PAT iteratively restores replaceable original words and selects improved candidates for perturbed positions using geometry-aware guidance.
The authors report benchmark and real-world evaluations showing effectiveness, semantic-preservation, and platform-validation results.

source_observation.claim: The method estimates semantic change using explicit adversarial and non-adversarial prototypes.

interpretation.claim: Explicit geometric reference points can support semantic-aware decisions when model internals and probability scores are unavailable.

application.claim: For hard-label black-box text transformations, use observable prediction feedback together with prototype-based semantic estimates to guide candidate selection.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond the evaluated attack setting or how it behaves under different semantic constraints.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the benchmark datasets, state-of-the-art models, evaluation metrics, attack budgets, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not name the industry-leading natural language processing platforms or specify the real-world evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, computational costs, failure cases, or comparison conditions.
